Main.sentence: Richard Bruce Cheney ( /ˈtʃeɪni/ ___E:CHAY-nee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key)___ ; [a] born January 30, 1941) is an American former politician and businessman who served as the 46th ___E:vice president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_the_United_States)___ from 2001 to 2009 under President ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ .
He has been called ___E:the most powerful vice president in American history U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_presidency_of_Dick_Cheney)___ .

Cheney previously served as ___E:White House Chief of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Chief_of_Staff)___ for President ___E:Gerald Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford)___ , the ___E:U.S. representative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._representative)___ for Wyoming's at-large congressional district from 1979 to 1989, and as the 17th ___E:United States secretary of defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_secretary_of_defense)___ in the administration of President ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ .
Born in ___E:Lincoln, Nebraska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln,_Nebraska)___ , Cheney grew up there and in ___E:Casper, Wyoming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casper,_Wyoming)___ .

He attended ___E:Yale University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University)___ before earning a Bachelor of Arts and Master of Arts in political science from the ___E:University of Wyoming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Wyoming)___ .

He began his political career as an intern for Congressman ___E:William A. Steiger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_A._Steiger)___ , eventually working his way into the ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ during the ___E:Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Richard_Nixon)___ and ___E:Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Gerald_Ford)___ administrations.

He served as ___E:White House chief of staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Chief_of_Staff)___ from 1975 to 1977. In 1978, he was elected to the ___E:U.S. House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ , and represented ___E:Wyoming's at-large congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming%27s_at-large_congressional_district)___ from 1979 to 1989, briefly serving as ___E:House minority whip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_whips_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ in 1989. He was appointed ___E:Secretary of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense)___ during the ___E:presidency of George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_George_H._W._Bush)___ , and held the position for most of Bush's term from 1989 to 1993.  As secretary, he oversaw ___E:Operation Just Cause U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Just_Cause)___ in 1989 and ___E:Operation Desert Storm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Desert_Storm)___ in 1991. While out of office during the ___E:Clinton administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Bill_Clinton)___ , he was the chairman and CEO of ___E:Halliburton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halliburton)___ from 1995 to 2000.

In ___E:July 2000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Republican_Party_vice_presidential_candidate_selection)___ , Cheney was chosen by presumptive ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ presidential nominee ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ as his running mate in the ___E:2000 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

They defeated their ___E:Democratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ opponents, incumbent vice president ___E:Al Gore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore)___ and senator ___E:Joe Lieberman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Lieberman)___ .

In ___E:2004 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election)___ , Cheney was reelected to his second term as vice president with Bush as president, defeating their Democratic opponents Senators ___E:John Kerry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry)___ and ___E:John Edwards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Edwards)___ .

During Cheney's tenure as vice president, he played a leading behind-the-scenes role in the ___E:George W. Bush administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_George_W._Bush)___ 's response to the ___E:September 11 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ and coordination of the ___E:Global War on Terrorism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_Terror)___ .

He was an early proponent of ___E:invading Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War)___ , alleging that the ___E:Saddam Hussein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein)___ regime possessed ___E:weapons of mass destruction U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weapon_of_mass_destruction)___ program and had an ___E:operational relationship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein_and_al-Qaeda_link_allegations)___ with ___E:Al-Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda)___ ; however, neither allegation was ever substantiated.

He also pressured the intelligence community to provide intelligence consistent with the administration's rationales for invading Iraq. Cheney was often criticized for the Bush administration's policies regarding the campaign against terrorism, for his support of ___E:wiretapping by the National Security Agency (NSA) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSA_warrantless_surveillance_controversy)___ and for his endorsement of the U.S.'s " ___E:enhanced interrogation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_interrogation_techniques)___ " ___E:torture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torture)___ program.

He publicly disagreed with President Bush's position against ___E:same-sex marriage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_the_United_States)___ in 2004,  but also said it is "appropriately a matter for the states to decide".
Cheney ended his vice presidential tenure as a deeply unpopular figure in American politics with an approval rating of 13 percent.
His peak approval rating in the wake of the September 11 attacks was 68 percent.

Since leaving the vice presidency, Cheney has been critical of modern Republican leadership, including ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ , going as far as to endorse Trump's challenger in ___E:2024 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election)___ , Democrat ___E:Kamala Harris U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris)___ .

He is the oldest living former U.S. vice president, following the death of ___E:Walter Mondale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Mondale)___ in 2021, as well as the most recent Vice President not to run for President.
Cheney was born in Lincoln, Nebraska, the son of Marjorie Lorraine (née Dickey) and Richard Herbert Cheney.
He is of predominantly English, as well as ___E:Welsh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_American)___ , Irish, and French Huguenot ancestry.

His father was a soil conservation agent for the ___E:U.S. Department of Agriculture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Agriculture)___ and his mother was a softball star in the 1930s;  Cheney was one of three children.

He attended ___E:Calvert Elementary School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvert_Elementary_School)___   before his family moved to ___E:Casper, Wyoming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casper,_Wyoming)___ ,  where he attended ___E:Natrona County High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natrona_County_High_School)___ .

He attended ___E:Yale University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University)___ , but by his own account had problems adjusting to the college, and dropped out.   Among the influential teachers from his days in New Haven was ___E:H. Bradford Westerfield U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._Bradford_Westerfield)___ , whom Cheney repeatedly credited with having helped to shape his approach to ___E:foreign policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_policy)___ .

He later attended the ___E:University of Wyoming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Wyoming)___ , where he earned both a Bachelor of Arts and a Master of Arts in ___E:political science U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_science)___ .

He subsequently started, but did not finish, ___E:doctoral U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctorate)___ studies in political science at the ___E:University of Wisconsin–Madison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Wisconsin%E2%80%93Madison)___ .
In November 1962, at the age of 21, Cheney was convicted of ___E:driving while intoxicated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_under_the_influence)___ (DWI).
He was arrested for DWI again the following year.  Cheney said that the arrests made him "think about where I was and where I was headed.
I was headed down a bad road if I continued on that course."
In 1964, he married ___E:Lynne Vincent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynne_Cheney)___ , his high school sweetheart, whom he had met at age 14.

When Cheney became eligible for the ___E:draft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription_in_the_United_States)___ , during the ___E:Vietnam War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War)___ , he applied for and received five draft deferments.

In 1989, The Washington Post writer George C. Wilson interviewed Cheney as the next ___E:secretary of defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Secretary_of_Defense)___ ; when asked about his deferments, Cheney reportedly said, "I had other priorities in the '60s than military service."  Cheney testified during his confirmation hearings in 1989 that he received deferments to finish a college career that lasted six years rather than four, owing to sub-par academic performance and the need to work to pay for his education.

Upon graduation, Cheney was eligible for the draft, but at the time, the ___E:Selective Service System U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selective_Service_System)___ was not inducting married men.  On October 26, 1965, the draft was expanded to include married men without children; Cheney's first daughter, ___E:Elizabeth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liz_Cheney)___ , was born 9 months and two days later.
Cheney's fifth and final deferment granted him "3-A" status, a "hardship" deferment available to men with dependents.
In January 1967, Cheney turned 26 and was no longer eligible for the draft.
In 1966 Cheney dropped out of the doctoral program at the University of Wisconsin to work as staff aide for Governor ___E:Warren Knowles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_P._Knowles)___ .
In 1968 Cheney was awarded an ___E:American Political Science Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Political_Science_Association)___ congressional fellowship and moved to Washington.

Cheney's political career began in 1969, as an intern for Congressman ___E:William A. Steiger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_A._Steiger)___ during the ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ Administration.

He then joined the staff of ___E:Donald Rumsfeld U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Rumsfeld)___ , who was then Director of the ___E:Office of Economic Opportunity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Economic_Opportunity)___ from 1969 to 1970.  He held several positions in the years that followed: White House Staff Assistant in 1971, Assistant Director of the Cost of Living Council from 1971 to 1973, and Deputy Assistant to the president from 1974 to 1975. As deputy assistant, Cheney suggested several options in a memo to Rumsfeld, including use of the ___E:US Justice Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Justice_Department)___ , that the ___E:Ford administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_administration)___ could use to limit damage from an article, published by The New York Times , in which investigative reporter ___E:Seymour Hersh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seymour_Hersh)___ reported that Navy submarines had tapped into Soviet undersea communications as part of a highly classified program, ___E:Operation Ivy Bells U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Ivy_Bells)___ .

Cheney was Assistant to the President and White House Deputy Chief of Staff under ___E:Gerald Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford)___ from December 1974 to November 1975.    When Rumsfeld was named ___E:Secretary of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Secretary_of_Defense)___ , Cheney became ___E:White House Chief of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Chief_of_Staff)___ , succeeding Rumsfeld.
He later was campaign manager for Ford's ___E:1976 presidential campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

In 1978, Cheney was elected to represent Wyoming in the ___E:U.S. House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ and succeeded retiring ___E:Democratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Democratic_Party)___ Congressman ___E:Teno Roncalio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teno_Roncalio)___ , having defeated his Democratic opponent, Bill Bagley.
Cheney was re-elected five times, serving until 1989. [citation needed]
In 1987, he was elected Chairman of the ___E:House Republican Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Republican_Conference)___ .
The following year, he was elected ___E:House Minority Whip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minority_Whip_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ .
He served for two and a half months before he was appointed Secretary of Defense instead of former U.S.
Senator ___E:John G. Tower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_G._Tower)___ , whose nomination had been rejected by the U.S.
Senate in March 1989.

He voted against the creation of the ___E:U.S. Department of Education U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Education)___ , citing his concern over budget deficits and expansion of the federal government, and claiming that the department was an encroachment on ___E:states' rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States%27_rights)___ .
He voted against funding ___E:Head Start U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_Start_Program)___ , but reversed his position in 2000.

Cheney initially opposed establishing a national holiday in honor of ___E:Martin Luther King Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr.)___ in 1979, but supported creation of ___E:Martin Luther King Jr. Day U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr._Day)___ five years later, in 1983.
Cheney supported ___E:Bob Michel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Michel)___ 's (R-IL) bid to become Republican Minority Leader.
In April 1980, Cheney endorsed Governor ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ for president, becoming one of Reagan's earliest supporters.

In 1986, after President ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ vetoed a bill to impose ___E:economic sanctions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_sanctions)___ on South Africa for its policy of ___E:apartheid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid)___ , Cheney was one of 83 Representatives to vote against overriding Reagan's veto.  In later years, he articulated his opposition to unilateral sanctions against many different countries, stating "they almost never work"  and that in that case they might have ended up hurting the people instead.

In 1986, Cheney, along with 145 Republicans and 31 Democrats, voted against a non-binding Congressional resolution calling on the South African government to release ___E:Nelson Mandela U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Mandela)___ from prison, after the Democrats defeated proposed amendments that would have required Mandela to renounce violence sponsored by the ___E:African National Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_National_Congress)___ (ANC) and requiring it to oust the communist faction from its leadership; the resolution was defeated.

Appearing on ___E:CNN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN)___ , Cheney addressed criticism for this, saying he opposed the resolution because the ANC "at the time was viewed as a terrorist organization and had a number of interests that were fundamentally inimical to the United States."
Originally declining, U.S.
Congressman ___E:Barber Conable U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barber_Conable)___ persuaded Cheney to join the moderate Republican Wednesday Group in order to move up the leadership ranks.

He was elected ___E:Chairman of the Republican Policy Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Policy_Committee_Chairman_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ from 1981 to 1987. Cheney was the Ranking Member of the Select Committee to investigate the ___E:Iran-Contra Affair U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran-Contra_Affair)___ .
He promoted Wyoming's petroleum and coal businesses as well.

President ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ nominated Cheney for the office of ___E:Secretary of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense)___ immediately after the U.S.
Senate failed to confirm ___E:John Tower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Tower)___ for that position.

The senate confirmed Cheney by a vote of 92 to 0  and he served in that office from March 1989 to January 1993. He directed the ___E:United States invasion of Panama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Panama)___ and ___E:Operation Desert Storm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Desert_Storm)___ in the Middle East. In 1991, he was awarded the ___E:Presidential Medal of Freedom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom)___ by Bush.   Later that year, he received the U.S.

Senator John Heinz Award for Greatest Public Service by an Elected or Appointed Official, an award given out annually by ___E:Jefferson Awards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Awards_for_Public_Service)___ .

Cheney has said his time at the Pentagon was the most rewarding period of his public service career, calling it "the one that stands out."  In 2014, Cheney recounted that when he met with President ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ to accept the offer, he passed a painting in the private residence entitled The Peacemakers, which depicted President Lincoln, General Grant, and ___E:William Tecumseh Sherman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Tecumseh_Sherman)___ . "My great-grandfather had served under William Tecumseh Sherman throughout the war," Cheney said, "and it occurred to me as I was in the room as I walked in to talk to the President about becoming Secretary of Defense, I wondered what he would have thought that his great-grandson would someday be in the White House with the President talking about taking over the reins of the U.S. military."

Cheney worked closely with ___E:Pete Williams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Williams_(television_correspondent))___ , ___E:Assistant Secretary of Defense for Public Affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_Secretary_of_Defense_for_Public_Affairs)___ , and ___E:Paul Wolfowitz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Wolfowitz)___ , ___E:Under Secretary of Defense for Policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Secretary_of_Defense_for_Policy)___ , from the beginning of his tenure.

He focused primarily on external matters, and left most of the internal DoD management to ___E:Deputy Secretary of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_Defense)___ ___E:Donald Atwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_J._Atwood_Jr.)___ .
Cheney's most immediate issue as Secretary of Defense was the ___E:Department of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense)___ budget.

Cheney deemed it appropriate to cut the budget and downsize the military, following the ___E:Reagan Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reagan_Administration)___ 's peacetime defense buildup at the height of the ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ .

As part of the fiscal year 1990 budget, Cheney assessed the requests from each of the branches of the armed services for such expensive programs as the ___E:Avenger II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonnell_Douglas_A-12_Avenger_II)___ Naval attack aircraft, the ___E:B-2 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-2_Spirit)___ stealth bomber, the ___E:V-22 Osprey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V-22_Osprey)___ tilt-wing ___E:helicopter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helicopter)___ , the ___E:Aegis destroyer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aegis_destroyer)___ and the ___E:MX missile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGM-118_Peacekeeper)___ , totaling approximately $4.5 billion in light of changed world politics.
Cheney opposed the V-22 program, which Congress had already appropriated funds for, and initially refused to issue contracts for it before relenting.

When the 1990 Budget came before Congress in the summer of 1989, it settled on a figure between the Administration's request and the ___E:House Armed Services Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Armed_Services_Committee)___ 's recommendation.

In subsequent years under Cheney, the proposed and adopted budgets followed patterns similar to that of 1990. Early in 1991, he unveiled a plan to reduce military strength by the mid-1990s to 1.6 million, compared with 2.2 million when he entered office.

Cheney's 1993 defense budget was reduced from 1992, omitting programs that Congress had directed the Department of Defense to buy weapons that it did not want, and omitting unrequested reserve forces.
Over his four years as Secretary of Defense, Cheney downsized the military and his budgets showed negative real growth, despite pressures to acquire weapon systems advocated by Congress.
The Department of Defense's total obligational authority in current dollars declined from $291 billion to $270 billion.

Total military personnel strength decreased by 19 percent, from about 2.2 million in 1989 to about 1.8 million in 1993.  Notwithstanding the overall reduction in military spending, Cheney directed the development of a Pentagon plan to ensure U.S. military dominance in the post-Cold War era.

Cheney publicly expressed concern that nations such as ___E:Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq)___ , ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran)___ , and ___E:North Korea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea)___ , could acquire nuclear components after the ___E:collapse of the Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collapse_of_the_Soviet_Union)___ in 1991. The end of the Cold War, the fall of the Soviet Union, and the disintegration of the ___E:Warsaw Pact U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Pact)___ obliged the first Bush Administration to reevaluate the ___E:North Atlantic Treaty Organization's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Atlantic_Treaty_Organization)___ (NATO's) purpose and makeup.

Cheney believed that NATO should remain the foundation of European security relationships and that it would remain important to the United States in the long term; he urged the alliance to lend more assistance to the new democracies in Eastern Europe.

Cheney's views on NATO reflected his skepticism about prospects for peaceful social development in the former ___E:Eastern Bloc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Bloc)___ countries, where he saw a high potential for political uncertainty and instability.

He felt that the Bush Administration was too optimistic in supporting ___E:General Secretary of the CPSU U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_CPSU)___ ___E:Mikhail Gorbachev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Gorbachev)___ and his successor, Russian President ___E:Boris Yeltsin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin)___ .
Cheney not only wanted the break-up of the USSR but also of Russia itself.
Cheney worked to maintain strong ties between the United States and its European allies.
Cheney persuaded the ___E:Kingdom of Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Saudi_Arabia)___ to allow bases for U.S. ground troops and war planes in the nation.
